question: What is the approximate total number of nephrons found inside one single healthy human kidney?
explanation: A healthy human kidney contains approximately one million nephrons working continuously to filter blood. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following describes the two main parts that make up every individual nephron?

options.A: The renal corpuscle and the renal tubule
options.B: The renal pelvis and the ureter
options.D: The renal artery and the renal vein

explanation: Every nephron is built from a renal corpuscle that filters blood and a renal tubule that processes the filtrate into urine. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h1)

question: What specialized cells with foot-like extensions form filtration slits around the glomerular capillaries?
explanation: Podocytes wrap around the capillaries of the glomerulus, creating filtration slits that help block large blood cells and proteins from escaping. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why is the pressure inside the glomerular capillaries much higher than in typical capillaries elsewhere in the body?

options.A: The entering arteriole is wider than the exiting arteriole
options.B: The heart pumps blood directly into the kidneys without branching
options.C: The renal veins are completely blocked by surrounding muscles
options.D: The surrounding Bowman's capsule squeezes the blood vessels tightly

explanation: The wider afferent arteriole brings blood in faster than the narrower efferent arteriole can take it out, building up the high pressure needed for filtration. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h2)

question: What microscopic feature on the cells of the proximal convoluted tubule greatly increases its surface area?
explanation: The microvilli form a brush border that maximizes the surface area for reabsorbing water and nutrients from the filtrate. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h3)

question: What happens to nearly all the glucose that is filtered out of the blood into the proximal convoluted tubule?

options.A: It is broken down into waste products and excreted
options.B: It is completely reabsorbed back into the bloodstream
options.C: It passes straight through into the final urine
options.D: It is stored inside the tubule cells as reserve fat

explanation: A healthy kidney reabsorbs almost 100 percent of filtered glucose back into the blood in the proximal convoluted tubule so none is lost in the urine. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which part of the Loop of Henle is freely permeable to water but does NOT let salt pass out?
explanation: The descending limb allows water to move out into the salty medulla while keeping solutes trapped inside, concentrating the fluid. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary role of the thick ascending limb of the Loop of Henle?

options.A: Adding large protein waste molecules to the filtrate
options.B: Reabsorbing all remaining glucose and amino acids
options.C: Actively pumping out salt without letting water follow
options.D: Slowing down the flow of urine to rest the kidney

explanation: The ascending limb pumps out ions like sodium and chloride to create the medullary concentration gradient while remaining impermeable to water. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which hormone acts on the distal convoluted tubule to increase the reabsorption of sodium ions?
explanation: Aldosterone targets the distal nephron to promote sodium retention and potassium excretion, helping maintain blood volume and pressure. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h5)

question: How does antidiuretic hormone (ADH) affect the cells of the collecting duct when a person is dehydrated?

options.A: It thickens the tubule walls to prevent any fluid from passing through
options.B: It blocks salt pumps to make the urine completely salt-free
options.C: It stops all filtration in the glomerulus to save body fluids
options.D: It causes water channels to be inserted, letting water leave the tubule

explanation: ADH triggers the insertion of aquaporins, allowing water to escape the collecting duct back into the body, resulting in concentrated urine. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which microscopic structure is primarily damaged during glomerulonephritis?

options.A: The simple squamous cells of the renal pelvis
options.B: The glomerular basement membrane and podocytes
options.C: The smooth muscle lining the ureter walls
options.D: The collecting duct aquaporin water channels

explanation: Glomerulonephritis involves inflammation and injury to the filtration barrier of the glomerulus, leading to protein and blood in the urine. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why does acute tubular necrosis cause a sharp drop in urine production?

options.A: All water is absorbed back into the bloodstream instantly
options.B: The glomerulus stops receiving blood from the renal artery entirely
options.C: Dead tubule cells break off and block the inside of the tubule
options.D: The bladder muscles become paralyzed by toxins

explanation: When tubule cells die in acute tubular necrosis, they detach and plug the tubular lumen, preventing urine from flowing through properly. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T2#BMP121_U3_T2_h6)
